keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Heroic Australian pub-rock anthem in C major built around the universal I - V - vi - IV progression
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: A minor is the relative minor of C major

mainProgression.description: The ultimate heroic four-chord progression: grounding the tonic in C, driving through G, dipping into the relative minor Am, before rising triumphant on F.

sectionProgressions.description: Relentless four-chord cycle building from an intimate acoustic whisper to an explosive stadium singalong
Minor detour through Dm and F adding narrative tension before the triumphant final chorus return

harmonicFunction: C (I) - Triumphant major tonic establishing the hero's quest and home foundation
G (V) - Dominant chord propelling the momentum forward with urgency
Am (vi) - Relative minor introducing adversity, emotional gravity, and reflection
F (IV) - Majestic subdominant lift providing the uplifting resolution at the end of each four-bar phrase
Dm (ii) - Supertonic minor introducing contrast in the reflective bridge

techniques.name: Stadium Anthem Strumming & Dynamic Arc
techniques.description: Building from a quiet, palm-muted acoustic verse to thunderous open-string stadium strums with full dynamic swing

notes: F: 1-3-3-2-1-1 or X-X-3-2-1-1 (Fmaj7 mini-barre)
sequence: Start the verse with delicate down-up acoustic strums near the bridge
Accent beats 2 and 4 to sync with the kick-and-snare backbeat
Unleash full-arm strums across all 6 strings when the horns and drums enter on the chorus
tips: If the full F barre chord is difficult, use the open Fmaj7 (X-X-3-2-1-0) or mini-barre (X-X-3-2-1-1)
Keep your strumming wrist relaxed to maintain steady 120 BPM pocket for 4 minutes
Dig in heavily on the G to Am transition to highlight the emotional minor shift

techniques.name: Brass-and-Guitar Octave Fanfare & Melodic Fills
techniques.description: Doubling the iconic French horn and brass fanfare lines with singing electric guitar melodies in C major, cutting through the stadium march

notes: Target C major scale notes: C (8th fret string 1), D (10th fret), E (12th fret), G (15th fret)
Step through the fanfare motif: 8th fret B -> 10th fret B -> 8th fret high E -> 10th fret high E -> 12th fret high E
Apply wide, celebratory finger vibrato on sustained notes
sequence: Enter during the instrumental break locking in unison with the horn section
Ascend the high E string with assertive pick dynamics
Resolve smoothly to the open C chord on beat 1 of the chorus
tips: Use a Telecaster bridge pickup for maximum bite through the dense horn arrangement
Add a touch of analog boost or overdrive for sustain without harsh fuzz
Coordinate your dynamic level so the guitar lifts the horns rather than overpowering them

sections.name: Intro Solo Acoustic Whisper
sections.description: Mark Seymour starts solitary with just a quiet, percussive acoustic guitar rhythm setting up the marching pulse.
notes: Play with gentle, controlled dynamics near the bridge
Clean transitions between open C, G, Am, and F cowboy shapes
Establish the steady 120 BPM marching pulse

sections.name: Verse 1 Four-Chord March
sections.description: The bass and light snare enter ('Woke up this morning from the strangest dream...'), locking into the iconic 120 BPM marching cadence.
notes: Keep the strumming even and rhythmic on beats 2 and 4
Let the F chord ring cleanly into each four-bar turnaround
Leave space for Mark Seymour's passionate narrative vocal

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Singalong
sections.description: The horns explode into the mix on 'And if you told me about the places you were goin' to...', driving thousands of AFL/NRL fans into a roaring chorus.
notes: Full-volume down-up stadium strumming across all six strings
Lock firmly into the 120 BPM marching tempo with the kick drum
Accentuate the transition into the Am chord to highlight the emotional minor color

sections.name: Bridge Reflective Minor Detour
sections.description: The triumphant march pauses for a poignant minor breakdown ('I followed you through rain and cold...'), building anticipation for the instrumental fanfare.
notes: Drop dynamic volume slightly on the Am to Em descent
Crescendo across the F and G chords with heavy downstrokes
Sets up the explosive return of the horn and guitar fanfare

sections.name: Horn Section Guitar Fanfare & Lead Fills
sections.description: Barry Palmer's electric guitar links up with the legendary Hunters & Collectors horn section to double the heroic instrumental theme in triumphant singing octaves and soaring major lead fills across the neck.
notes: Start on the B string (8th and 10th frets) and ascend to the high E string (8th, 10th, and 12th frets)
Lock in tight unison with the brass fanfare melody
Add rich finger vibrato on sustained high notes
Resolve cleanly into the ringing open C cowboy chord

sections.name: Final Triumphant Chorus & Outro Climax
sections.description: Maximum stadium power as the entire ensemble, horns, and roaring crowd vocals deliver the final 'I was searchin' for the Holy Grail!' climax.
sections.progression: C - G - Am - F (repeating to final C)
notes: Deliver full-arm acoustic and electric strums with unstoppable momentum
Climb up to the 15th-fret high G note for the soaring final fill
Hit the final sustained C major chord and let the brass and feedback ring

guitar.pickup: Acoustic dreadnought mic'd or bridge single-coil electric cut

amp.recommended: Fender Twin Reverb or Marshall JCM800 (clean with edge)

effects.distortion: Light transparent overdrive for electric rhythm tracks
effects.reverb: Large hall reverb capturing the stadium atmosphere

beginner.title: Mastering the Four Chords
steps: Learn open C, G, Am, and F (or Fmaj7)
Practice smooth transitions at 90 BPM with a metronome
Memorize the I - V - vi - IV sequence
beginner.goals: Smooth chord changes without pauses or buzzing strings

intermediate.title: Dynamic Arc & Strumming Energy
steps: Build from quiet verse finger-strumming to full stadium chorus power
Lock into 120 BPM using our Metronome tool
Clean up the barre on the full F major chord
intermediate.goals: Compelling live performance capturing Mark Seymour's raw intensity

advanced.title: Horn Section Guitar Emulation
steps: Learn the soaring electric guitar octave lines reinforcing the brass fanfare
Master the driving syncopated rhythm accents in the bridge
Perform the complete song with vocal singalong projection
advanced.goals: Stage-ready live performance of Australia's definitive sporting & pub anthem

commonMistakes: Starting the verse too loudly, leaving no room to build into the chorus
Struggling with the jump from Am to the full F major barre chord
Rushing past the 120 BPM tempo during the emotional climax
practiceRoutine: Warm up with 5 minutes of C - G - Am - F changes with a metronome
Practice the Am to F transition 15 times cleanly
Play through the entire track focusing on dynamic control from verse 1 to the final outro
focusAreas: Clean F major barre chord fretting
metronomeWork: Set click to 100 BPM to ensure clean chord landings on beat 1
Ramp up to 120 BPM with our Metronome Speed Trainer
Practice keeping steady time through the bridge without rushing
